conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you came in because your dialysis access in your left arm stopped working?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that's right. I felt the thrill yesterday morning, but by the time I got to dialysis, it was gone. They said the fistula was clotted.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You’ve had this fistula for a while and it’s been working well up until now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, about six months. No problems until now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve reviewed your imaging. There’s a clot in the cephalic vein, and also a narrowing near where it joins the subclavian vein. We did a procedure today to clear the clot and open up that narrowed area with a balloon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Did it work?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We were able to restore most of the flow, and you had a thrill again at the end of the procedure. But because the vein is small and there’s still some clot clinging to the wall, we’re watching you closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I’ll need dialysis soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re planning for dialysis tomorrow morning. But we’ll keep an eye on your arm overnight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, thanks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I’m checking on you. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m okay, but my arm still doesn’t feel right. No thrill this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I checked, and the fistula has clotted again. We’re going to try to clear it one more time, but we also need a backup plan for dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? Why did it clot so fast?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The vein is narrow and small, which makes it prone to clotting. We’ll try to open it again, but we’ll also place a tunneled dialysis catheter in your neck so we can use that if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: In my neck? Is that safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s a common procedure. We use ultrasound to guide the placement, and it’s very effective for dialysis when the fistula isn’t working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I trust you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We finished the procedure. We tried to clear the clot again, but the fistula remains blocked. The tunneled catheter in your left neck is in place and working well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can’t use my arm anymore?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. The fistula may need further evaluation. For now, we’ll use the catheter for dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this catheter before. It’s not ideal long-term, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're right. Catheters are more prone to infection and clotting. We’ll keep working on your fistula, but for now, this is the safest way to get you dialyzed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You mentioned some belly pain and nausea earlier. How’s that now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still a bit bloated. I threw up once.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did an X-ray of your abdomen. There’s stool in your colon and one loop of bowel is a bit dilated, but no blockage. We gave you a suppository to help move things along.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. I haven’t had a good bowel movement in a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s likely the cause. We’ll keep an eye on it and encourage fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your belly pain is better today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, much better. I had a bowel movement last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We also did a chest X-ray to check the catheter. The tip is in the right spot, no pneumothorax.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I saw something about nodules in my lungs?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we saw some small spots, but we repeated the X-ray with markers and confirmed they’re just your nipples. Nothing to worry about.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, really? I was worried it was something serious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, completely benign. We just wanted to be sure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had your dialysis this morning and you’re doing well. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. What about my arm?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The fistula still has no bruit or thrill. You’ll need to follow up with the access clinic to see if it can be salvaged. For now, you’ll use the catheter for dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my belly issue?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Resolved. Just keep up with fluids and fiber.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, doctor. I appreciate everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Make sure to keep your follow-up appointments and call if you have fever, redness at the catheter site, or any concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do.
